content: These continuous legislative adjustments underscore the absolute necessity for service providers to maintain vigilant monitoring of ICASA’s announcements to ensure their operational strategies align with current eligibility criteria and application procedures. Quantitative data indicates an overall increasing trend in processing durations for more complex regulatory approvals. The maximum estimated processing time currently reaches 120.0 days for a Radio Frequency Spectrum License. This extended duration reflects the intricate technical evaluation, interference analysis, and regulatory scrutiny applied to spectrum allocation, which is a finite and highly contested national resource. Conversely, the minimum estimated processing time is 30.0 days for a Class Electronic Communications Network Service (CECNS) license. This type approval framework is a critical component of the broader compliance landscape, as failure to meet these technical requirements can result in severe regulatory penalties and the confiscation of non-compliant equipment [75] . While this process primarily addresses the certification of specific hardware rather than broader entity operational licensing, it remains an unavoidable prerequisite for deploying any network infrastructure [75] . Furthermore, ICASA has been actively pursuing consumer-centric policies that impact service structuring, including the formulation of mandatory data carry-over rules slated for implementation in 2027, which will heavily influence how service providers package and contract their telecommunications offerings [74] . To successfully navigate the multifaceted ICASA licensing requirements, businesses must engage in proactive and highly structured compliance management. Insights from ICASA’s Annual Performance Plan for the 2026-2027 financial year indicate that the authority’s operational focus is heavily weighted toward compliance oversight and the systematic collection of regulatory fees [74] . Given that public regulatory announcements on social media platforms and initial press releases frequently lack granular details regarding specific application fees, technical guidelines, or procedural steps, direct consultation with the authority is often required to obtain comprehensive operational directives [56] [72] .
